title: 2D and 3D Wavefronts: Diffraction
seo_title: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: 2D and 3D Wavefronts: Diffraction Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Wavefronts and Huygens' principle; diffraction of waves through a single slit; the relationship between the degree of diffraction, the slit width and the wavelength; interference of light as evidence for the wave nature of light. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Physics: 2D and 3D wavefronts)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): wavefronts, Huygens' principle, diffraction through a single slit and interference. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets.
key_sub: Diffraction is greatest when the slit width is close to the wavelength.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wavefront is a line joining points of a wave that are in phase, such as crests. Huygens' principle says that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of circular wavelets; the new wavefront is the line that touches them all.

Diffraction is the spreading of waves through an opening or around an obstacle. The degree of diffraction increases as the wavelength increases or the slit becomes narrower. Light shows diffraction and interference patterns, which is evidence that light behaves as a wave.

Example

Which diffracts more through a narrow slit, red or blue light?

Red has the longer wavelength.

Answer: red light

Example

The slit is made narrower. What happens to the central band?

Degree of diffraction ∝ λ/w

Answer: it becomes wider

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a wider slit gives more diffraction.
  • Mixing up diffraction and refraction.
  • Thinking only light can diffract.

faq.q: Why can you hear people around a corner but not see them?
faq.a: Sound waves have long wavelengths, similar to the size of a doorway, so they diffract a lot; light waves are far too short.
